title: 6.6.21 Fix the Broken Pseudocode: the Pause State
description: Repair half-finished pseudocode for a pause feature: give the not-playing frame its own branch, wire in the pause screen, stop a step jumping to itself, and add the way out.

steps.title: Repair the half-finished pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is what the finished feature should do, in plain English:

**1.** When the state is play: update the game, and if p was pressed, change the state to paused.

**2.** When the state is not play (it is paused): draw the pause screen, and if p was pressed, change the state back to play.

**3.** Every path ends at the end of the frame. No step may send you back to itself.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

Someone started this pseudocode and stopped halfway. It is already in `README.md`. **Press Run before changing anything**: four checks should be red. Then repair it, do not start over:

- Give the play decision its own **ELSE** branch, for every frame that is not playing.
- Move `CALL drawPauseScreen` into that branch so it runs only when paused.
- Remove the **GO TO**. Setting a state is an ordinary step: the frame carries on to the end.
- Inside the ELSE branch, add the way out: if p is pressed, SET state TO "play".

When it is all green, check the thing no check covers: can the player get out of pause? Green means legal, not finished.
hints: A step that jumps back to itself is a hung game, written down. Delete the GO TO line.
The ELSE branch runs on every frame that is not playing, so that is where drawPauseScreen belongs.

requirements.title: The play decision has an ELSE
requirements.description: An ELSE branch for every frame that is not playing.
requirements.hint: Give the IF state is "play" an ELSE branch, for the frames when the game is not playing.

requirements.title: drawPauseScreen is in the ELSE branch
requirements.description: CALL drawPauseScreen after the ELSE, so it runs only when paused.
requirements.hint: Move CALL drawPauseScreen under the ELSE, so it floats nowhere and runs only on the paused frames.

requirements.title: No step jumps back to itself
requirements.description: No GO TO or loop back. A state change is an ordinary step.
requirements.hint: Delete the GO TO line. Setting the state does its one job, then the frame goes on to the end.

requirements.title: A way out of pause
requirements.description: In the ELSE branch, IF p is pressed then SET state TO "play".
requirements.hint: In the ELSE branch add IF p is pressed, with SET state TO "play" inside it, so the player can leave pause.

requirements.title: Pausing sits inside the p check
requirements.description: SET state TO "paused" is inside an IF p is pressed.
requirements.hint: SET state TO "paused" belongs inside IF p is pressed.

requirements.title: Playing updates the game
requirements.description: CALL updateGame in the play branch.
requirements.hint: The play branch should CALL updateGame.

flowchart LR
  A([draw runs]) --> B{state is play}
  B -- yes --> C[[updateGame]]
  C --> D{p pressed}
  D -- yes --> E[state = paused]
  D -- no --> Z([end of frame])
  E --> Z
  B -- no --> F[[drawPauseScreen]]
  F --> G{p pressed}
  G -- yes --> H[state = play]
  G -- no --> Z
  H --> Z
planChart.caption: The finished pause feature. The not-playing branch draws the pause screen and has a way back to play.
